articles.title: What Is Inside an Egg?
articles.dek: You eat eggs all the time. But do you know all the parts inside one?

sources.name: Virginia Cooperative Extension: Parts of an egg
British Egg Information Service: Brown vs white eggs

paras: You eat eggs for breakfast, in cakes and in noodles. But have you ever looked carefully inside one? An egg is more than a yellow middle and a white part. There are lots of parts, and each part has a job. Let's crack an egg open and find out what is there.

First, there is the shell. It is hard, but it breaks easily. The shell is made of calcium carbonate. This is the same stuff as chalk. A chicken's eggshell has got about 7,000 tiny holes in it. You can't see them, but air goes in and out through them.

Under the shell, there are two thin skins. They are called membranes. They keep dirt and bacteria out of the egg. At the big, round end of the egg, the two skins come apart. There is a small pocket of air between them. This is the air cell. When an egg gets older, the air cell gets bigger.
Next, there is the egg white. It is mostly water and protein. Protein is good for your body. In a raw egg, the white isn't white at all. It is clear, like water! It only turns white when you cook it.

In the middle, there is the yolk. It is yellow or orange, and it has got all the fat in the egg. Look closely at a raw egg, and you can see two short white strings. There is one on each side of the yolk. They hold the yolk in the middle of the egg.

Some eggs are brown, and some are white. Is a brown egg better for you? No, it isn't. The colour of the shell depends on the hen. Brown hens usually lay brown eggs, and white hens usually lay white eggs. There are no differences in the food inside. Some hens even lay blue eggs!

articles.title: A Week with a Table Tennis Player
articles.dek: Aiko plays table tennis five days a week. How does she do it?
paras: Every week, our school magazine talks to a student with an interesting hobby. This week, Tom Becker from Year 8 met Aiko Tanaka. She is fourteen, and she plays table tennis for our town's team.

Tom: When do you practise, Aiko? Aiko: I practise five days a week, from Monday to Friday. I always go to the sports centre straight after school. I usually play for two hours. On Saturdays, I often have matches in other towns.

Tom: What do you do in a training session? Aiko: First, I run and do some exercises. Then my coach, Mr Silva, gives me different balls. Sometimes he hits the ball very fast. Sometimes he hits it very slowly with a lot of spin. The ball turns round and round, so it's hard to hit back. I need to watch it carefully all the time.

Tom: Do you ever feel tired? Aiko: Yes, sometimes! On Thursdays I have a lot of homework, so I often go to bed late. But I never miss training. My coach says that good players come back every day. I hardly ever watch TV in the week.

Tom: What do you eat before a match? Aiko: I usually eat rice, chicken and vegetables. I never eat chips or sweets before I play. They make me feel slow. I always take a big bottle of water with me, because the hall is often very hot.

Tom: How do you feel when you lose? Aiko: I feel sad, of course. I sometimes cry in the changing room! But my mum always says, 'Learn one thing from every match.' So after a match, I write in a small notebook. I write what I did well and what I did badly.

Tom: What's your dream? Aiko: I want to play for my country one day. But first, I want to win the city competition in March. And I want more students to try table tennis. It's fast, it's fun, and you don't need a big field!

articles.title: Builders in Our Kitchen!
articles.dek: Marco's kitchen is usually quiet and warm. This week, it's full of noise and dust.
paras: Hi everyone, it's Marco! Usually our kitchen is my favourite room. We eat there, I do my homework there, and Dad often plays music there on Sunday mornings. But this week everything is different. Builders are working in our kitchen!

Our kitchen is very old, so my parents are making it new. Right now, two builders are taking out the old cupboards. They are making a lot of noise. Every morning they arrive at eight o'clock, and they usually leave at five.

So where are we cooking this week? We aren't cooking at all! We're eating sandwiches and salads for lunch. Grandma lives near us, so we're having dinner at her flat every evening. She usually cooks fish on Tuesdays, and it's delicious!

The fridge is standing in the living room now. It looks very strange next to the sofa! Our cat, Pepper, doesn't like the builders. She usually sleeps on a chair in the kitchen. This week she's hiding under my bed all day.

There's dust everywhere. Mum cleans the floor every evening, but in the morning it's dirty again. The water isn't working in the kitchen, so we're washing the plates in the bathroom! My little sister thinks it's funny. I don't!

As I'm writing this, I can hear a loud drill. But I'm trying to be happy, because the new kitchen looks great in the pictures. It has got a big window and a long table. The builders say it will be ready next Friday.
Do you ever have builders at your home? What do you do? Tell me in the comments!

grammar.rule: Use the present simple for habits and things that are usually true (every day, usually, often). Use the present continuous (am / is / are + -ing) for things happening now or only for a short time (now, right now, this week).
table: She usually sleeps in the kitchen.
Right now, they are taking out the cupboards.
Mum cleans the floor every evening.
This week she's hiding under my bed.

examples.text: Builders are working in our kitchen!
Every morning they arrive at eight o'clock, and they usually leave at five.
She usually sleeps on a chair in the kitchen.
This week she's hiding under my bed all day.

items.why: Listen! means it is happening now: are painting.
On Sundays is a habit, and my dad = he: cooks.

items.q: Mum isn't here. She ___ to the shop right now.
We usually ___ in the kitchen, but this week we're eating in the garden.
items.why: Usually is a habit, so use the present simple: eat.

items.q: ___ your cat often sleep on your bed?
items.why: Often is a habit, and your cat = it: Does … sleep?

items.q: I ___ this blog because I want to tell you about my week.
items.why: It is happening now, so use am + writing.

kps.fact: This week, builders are making Marco's family's old kitchen new.
kps.q: Why are builders at Marco's house?

kps.fact: The builders arrive at eight and usually leave at five.
This week the family is having dinner at Grandma's flat.
kps.q: Where is the family having dinner this week?

kps.fact: Pepper the cat usually sleeps in the kitchen, but now she is hiding under Marco's bed.
The kitchen water isn't working, so they are washing the plates in the bathroom.
kps.q: Where are they washing the plates?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the text.
summary.model: Builders are making a new kitchen at Marco's house, so the family is eating at Grandma's this week. It's noisy, but the new kitchen looks great.

options.t: Builders are working in Marco's kitchen this week.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraphs 1 and 2.
options.evidence: Builders are working in our kitchen!

options.t: The family can't cook at home, so they are eating in other ways.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraph 3.

options.t: Home is noisy and dirty now, but the new kitchen looks great.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraphs 5 and 6.
options.evidence: But I'm trying to be happy, because the new kitchen looks great in the pictures.

options.t: Grandma usually cooks fish on Tuesdays.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: She usually cooks fish on Tuesdays, and it's delicious!

options.t: Marco's dad is helping the builders.
Pepper the cat loves the builders.
options.why: Wrong: Pepper doesn't like the builders.
options.evidence: Our cat, Pepper, doesn't like the builders.

speak.p: What is your favourite room at home? What do you usually do there?
speak.hint: My favourite room is … / I usually … there because …

write.p: Your friend wants to visit you this week, but builders are working in your house. Write a message to your friend. Write 25 words or more.
steps: Say what the builders are doing.
Say why your friend can't come this week.
Say when your friend can come.
